name: Tripoli
notes: The Autodromo di Mellaha, laid out on the salt flats east of Tripoli and home to the Tripoli Grand Prix from 1934 to 1940. Roughly rectangular and almost entirely flat out, its 13.14 km of sweeping curves and long straights made it the fastest road circuit of its day: Hermann Lang won here on 9 May 1937 at 212.5 km/h, giving the new Mercedes-Benz W125 victory on its debut, while Hans Stuck's Auto Union Type C set the lap record at 3m25.73s, an average of 229.9 km/h. A white concrete control tower faced a grandstand holding ten thousand spectators, and the circuit had both starting lights and photo-electric timing. The site later became Wheelus Air Base.
